CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit to reassess treatment efficacy for generalized anxiety disorder, insomnia, persistent fatigue, and tension-type headaches. Emphasis on evaluating symptom control, medication adherence, and any emerging concerns since the last visit.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his scheduled follow-up appointment, expressing a mixed review of his current treatment regimen. He reports a modest reduction in anxiety symptoms, with fewer episodes of irritability, particularly during high-stress work situations. He remains compliant with sertraline at 300 mg daily, yet he continues to experience cognitive challenges, specifically related to memory and focus, which he describes as hazy and distracting during work hours.
The frequency of his tension-type headaches has remained stable, occurring twice weekly with an intensity ranging from 4 to 6 out of 10. Mr. Smith notes that while topiramate at 150 mg daily has provided some relief, he has continued to rely on ibuprofen, utilizing it approximately four times a month due to persistent headache episodes. He attributes some exacerbation of headaches to ongoing work-related stress and fatigue.
Sleep patterns remain consistent, with Mr. Smith averaging 7 to 8 hours of sleep per night, aided by trazodone and melatonin. However, he reports that morning grogginess persists, which he identifies as a significant barrier to initiating daily activities. Mr. Smith has continued to engage in short walks during work breaks, which he believes have positively impacted his overall energy levels.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 300 mg daily (continued) 2. Trazodone 75 mg at bedtime (continued) 3. Lisinopril 10 mg daily (continued) 4. Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief (no change in frequency) 5. Amitriptyline 50 mg nightly (continued) 6. Topiramate 150 mg daily (continued) 7. Lorazepam 1 mg as needed (continued) 8. Melatonin 3 mg at bedtime (continued) 9. Modafinil 100 mg in the morning (continued)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith remains committed to regular physical activity, including brisk walking and hiking on weekends. He has maintained a balanced diet and continues to monitor his caffeine intake, which he believes is beneficial for managing his anxiety. His mindfulness practices, including meditation and yoga, are integral to his routine, although he acknowledges that work-related stress occasionally hinders his engagement in these activities.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Slight improvement in anxiety; persistent cognitive difficulties noted; sleep quality satisfactory; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms. - Neurological: Stable headache frequency; no dizziness or visual disturbances reported. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Fatigue remains manageable, particularly with modafinil, with no fever or significant weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 120/78 mmHg, HR 70 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.6F - General: Alert, oriented; appears mildly fatigued but engaged; mood appears anxious with moderate distress. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed; no tenderness in the temporal region. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears anxious with moderate distress.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 300 mg daily. Encourage ongoing cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) to address residual irritability and cognitive concerns. Reassess in one month for potential dose adjustments if symptoms do not continue to improve. 2. Insomnia: Continue trazodone at 75 mg at bedtime and melatonin 3 mg nightly; reassess in one month for efficacy and any side effects. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Continue topiramate at 150 mg daily; maintain headache diary to monitor frequency and intensity. If no improvement is noted in the next month, consider referral to a neurologist for further evaluation. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Continue modafinil at 100 mg in the morning; monitor for efficacy in alleviating fatigue symptoms. Reinforce the importance of stress management techniques and lifestyle modifications, including regular physical activity and adequate hydration.
Follow-up appointment is scheduled for 2029-08-22 to evaluate symptom progression, medication effectiveness, and discuss any new concerns. Mr. Smith is encouraged to maintain open communication regarding his treatment response and any lifestyle changes he implements.
